name: security-zero-trust
notes: Narrow, deep evidence: the case-competition bullet names Zero Trust and NIST SP 800-207 explicitly, but it was a design proposal, not operational security work. A good analyzer credits the named frameworks while keeping hands-on operational security (pentesting, SIEM, incident response) in missing. Tests that the model does not over-generalise one strong bullet into a whole security background.
jd:
Security Engineer I

Support our zero-trust rollout and security architecture reviews.

Requirements:
- Zero Trust architecture concepts
- Familiarity with NIST security frameworks
- Network segmentation
- Python scripting

Nice to have:
- SIEM tooling (Splunk, Elastic)
- Penetration testing
- Incident response experience
- Security certifications (Security+, CISSP)
